records.name: Centro Nueva Creación
records.summary: A nonprofit founded in 1995 in the Fairhill area. It runs an after school program for elementary students, a summer camp, and arts and photography projects rooted in Latino culture.
records.what_you_do: Elementary students join the weekday after school program for a snack, homework help, and arts projects, or take part in the summer camp or the Goodlands photography project. The summer camp includes breakfast and lunch, swimming, and weekly field trips, and ends with a public show of student work. Families call or email to ask about enrollment.

schedule.text: After school runs Monday to Friday, 3 to 6 pm, September through June. The site does not list summer camp dates.

cost.text: A sponsorship appeal on the site mentions a $95 fee for a semester of after school. No full fee schedule is posted, so call to confirm. Summer camp cost is not listed.

first_step.how: Call 215-426-8762 to ask about after school enrollment or summer camp. The site invites visitors to come by, but it does not explain how to set up a visit.
first_step.basis: The site invites families to call or visit, but it does not explain how enrollment works, what it costs, or when a new student can start.
first_step.what_to_expect: The after school program runs 3 to 6 pm on weekdays, September through June, and serves more than 50 elementary students a year. Each afternoon has a healthy snack, 15 minutes of play, about 45 minutes of homework help or tutoring, and about 45 minutes of arts projects with teaching artists. The arts projects use poetry, photography, drumming, and dance to explore family traditions and Latino culture. The site does not list a current fee.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-426-8762 before you come, since the site does not explain visits or enrollment steps.
The center is at 185 W. Tioga St., 19140.

records.notes: Name now uses the accent the group uses on its own pages. Tier 1 had no address; 185 W. Tioga St. (zip 19140) comes from the group's contact page, which also lists 215-426-8762. The contact email is obscured on the site, so none is recorded. Summer camp dates, ages and cost are not published. The Goodlands photography project appears on the exhibitions page, but no page read explains how to join it. The tier 1 cost came from a sponsorship appeal and stays marked as possibly out of date.

records.name: Chestnut Hill Tree Tenders
records.summary: A volunteer group in Chestnut Hill that plants free street trees twice a year, supported by the Chestnut Hill Community Association and the Pennsylvania Horticultural Society.
records.what_you_do: Deliver and plant street trees on planting days, and help the tree committee. The host property must give volunteers access to water and mulch on planting day, and the owner waters the tree, especially in its first year.

schedule.text: Trees are planted twice a year, in April and November, on planting days set by the co-chairs.

cost.text: The trees are free. The household that gets one waters it and gives volunteers access on planting day.

first_step.how: Contact a Tree Tender co-chair listed on the group's Tree Tenders page, or send the general volunteer form on the Chestnut Hill Community Association site, to join the committee or a planting day. To get a tree, apply online through the Pennsylvania Horticultural Society.
first_step.basis: Anyone can contact a co-chair or use the general volunteer form, and the page posts the planting months openly.
first_step.what_to_expect: On a planting day, volunteers deliver bareroot trees and plant them at properties that were approved to receive one. The host must give volunteers access to water and mulch that day. The page does not say what time a planting starts or how long it lasts, so ask a co-chair.
first_visit_tips: If a tree is going in at your property, give volunteers access to water and mulch on planting day.
A tree application must be accepted by both the Pennsylvania Horticultural Society and the City, which checks that utilities and easements are clear.

records.notes: Contact details now follow the general Chestnut Hill Community Association line and info address published on its volunteer page. Tier 1 had a city registered community organization email, phone and contact name (Anne McNiff), which do not appear on the group's pages, so the contact name was dropped; please check. The Tree Tenders page names two co-chairs with personal contact details, which were not copied. The tree page's dated items are from 2025 (a planting on November 15, 2025, and an April 2026 application deadline of November 1, 2025), so last sign of life moved from the tier 1 date of 2026-10, which came from a city zoning dataset. Status stays active because 2025-11 is within the last 12 months. The April planting date is written without a year on the page. Pennsylvania Horticultural Society is named as a partner.

records.name: Chestnut Street Singers
records.summary: A cooperative chamber choir that sings a wide range of music, from Renaissance works to new pieces. Singers are unpaid volunteers who audition, rehearse on Monday evenings, and perform two concerts a season.
records.what_you_do: Audition to join the choir, then rehearse and sing in the two concerts each season. Singers also help run the group, and the page lists roles such as receptions, graphics, and marketing for members.

schedule.text: Rehearsals run Mondays, 7 to 9 pm, at Children's Community School, in a fall cycle from late August to early November and a spring cycle from late January to early May. The choir gives two concerts a season.

locations.label: Concerts at the Church of the Holy Trinity

cost.text: Singers pay no participation fee, and the choir is run by volunteers. Singers who face money problems can ask for help in confidence, case by case, but help is not guaranteed.

first_step.how: Submit the audition application form on the group's Auditions page, or email auditions@chestnutstreetsingers.org to ask when the next audition window opens. To hear the choir first, look for the November 14, 2026 concert at 7 pm at the Church of the Holy Trinity; the page does not say how tickets are sold.
first_step.basis: Joining needs an application form and a short audition, and the page says not every applicant is auditioned, so the way in is selective.
first_step.what_to_expect: An audition lasts about 20 minutes. You sing scales to show your range, sing a short excerpt from a set piece with ensemble members, sight-read a passage, and talk briefly about why you want to join. Rehearsals then run Monday evenings for two hours at the school, with two concerts each season.
first_visit_tips: Learn measures 1 to 19 of the set excerpt from the score linked on the audition page before you go.
Rehearsals are Monday evenings, 7 to 9 pm, at the school at 1212 S 47th St.
You may miss no more than two rehearsals in a cycle, so check the dates before you apply.

records.notes: Tier 1 said this season's audition dates had passed and a spring window was undated. The auditions page now lists August 3 or August 10 audition dates with no year written, so treat them as past until the group confirms. No spring window is dated. The fall and spring cycles leave gaps, so the season field is left out. The tier 1 claim that concerts are open to all could not be confirmed (the page does not say), so it was removed. Concert ticketing is not described. The page does not say whether non-singers can volunteer, only that member roles exist. The concert venue is the Church of the Holy Trinity, not the rehearsal school.

records.name: Choral Arts Philadelphia
records.summary: A choir that has sung in Philadelphia since 1982, with most singers volunteers. It gives a season of concerts from October to May, mostly in Rittenhouse Square churches, with holiday programs such as Carols by Candlelight.
records.what_you_do: Sing in the choir after an audition, usher or greet at concerts, help with events or office work, or attend a concert. Volunteers can also help through the group's Volunteer page.

schedule.text: Concerts run from about October to May each season, with a holiday concert, Carols by Candlelight, in December.

locations.label: Concert venue: Church of the Holy Trinity
Concert venue: Saint Mark's Episcopal Church
Concert venue: Saint Patrick's Catholic Church

cost.text: Concert tickets are sold for each show, and a subscription for three to five concerts starts at $115 for the 2026 to 27 season. The page lists no dues for singers.

first_step.how: Email the group at the address under Audition Announcement on the Auditions page, with your voice part and singing experience. To see the choir first, buy a ticket to a 2026 to 27 concert from the season page.
first_step.basis: Joining means emailing to request an audition, and the page says most volunteer singers have music training or college singing. Concerts are open to ticket buyers.
first_step.what_to_expect: A first visit is a concert at one of three churches near Rittenhouse Square, with start times of 4 pm or 5 pm. You buy tickets online for one show or a subscription. The auditions page does not describe what an audition involves, so ask by email before you apply.
first_visit_tips: Check the start time on each concert, since the holiday concert starts at 5 pm.
A subscription lets you pick three to five concerts, and subscribers get seats held for New Year's Eve and Carols by Candlelight.

records.notes: The season page gives concert dates without a year for two shows (October 17 and December 5), and the season is labeled 2026 to 27, so no year is written for those dates. The audition page gives no audition length, dates, rehearsal days or rehearsal location, and the group's pages do not describe them. The audition email address is obscured in the page text, so it is not recorded. The group's mailing and office address is the Land Title Building, 100 South Broad Street, which is not a meeting place. A web search returned only the same pages. Subscriptions start at $115, per the season page.

records.name: The Clay Studio
records.summary: A ceramics studio with classes for beginners through advanced makers, kids' summer camps, free public clay sessions, and a gallery and shop open to visitors. Tuition help and a sliding scale are available.
records.what_you_do: Take a handbuilding or wheel class, join a workshop or summer camp, come to a free Hands on Clay session, or visit the gallery and shop. The second Thursday of each month brings extended evening hours, from 5 to 8 pm.

schedule.text: Classes run in terms of 5, 8 or 10 weeks, year round, on weekdays and some weekend mornings. Gallery and shop hours are weekdays 11 am to 5:30 pm and weekends 11 am to 5 pm. Clay and Conversations talks are on Thursdays at 1:30 pm, as scheduled.

cost.text: Class prices are not shown on the class list. Tuition assistance for classes, workshops and camps needs a short application. A sliding scale with three options (Community Supported, Standard, or Clay It Forward) needs no application, and you choose what to pay. Payment plans require a $100 non-refundable deposit.

access.notes: Step-free entry, and an elevator serves all floors. Restrooms are accessible on every floor, and water fountains are accessible on floors 2 to 4. Service dogs are welcome, and guided tours can be arranged ahead to suit needs. Nearest SEPTA: the Market-Frankford Line to Girard station, about a 10 minute walk. Bus 5 stops at 2nd and Girard, about a 6 minute walk, and bus 57 stops at Germantown Avenue and Master Street, about a 3 minute walk.

requirements.gear: Clay is bought at the studio's school store, and most adult classes do not supply personal tools.

first_step.how: Sign up for a class online on the studio's class page, or call 215-925-3453 extension 106. To try clay first, watch for a free Hands on Clay session, which is open to all ages.
first_step.basis: Beginner classes are listed with online sign up, a waitlist and a sliding scale, and free clay sessions are open to all ages. Classes do not take drop-ins.
first_step.what_to_expect: Adult classes run in terms of 5, 8 or 10 weeks, and each meets on one weekday for about three hours. In the fall term, Intro to Handbuilding meets Wednesday evenings from 6:30 to 9:30 pm, and Intro to Wheel Throwing meets Wednesday mornings from 10 am to 1 pm. Students buy their clay at the school store.
first_visit_tips: Clay must be bought at the school store, so pick it up there before your first session.
Open studio is only for enrolled students, so you need a class before you can use the studio on your own.
Drop-in visits to classes are not allowed, so sign up for the term before you come.

records.notes: The class list shows eight adult fall classes with weekday times, but the page gives no year with the dates, so none is written. Tier 1 placed the studio in Kensington; the page gives only the 19122 address, so the summary does not name a neighborhood. The visit page does not use the word wheelchair. Wheelchair is set to yes from its stated step-free entry and elevator access. The class policies say the 5 week Intro to Wheel class includes clay and basic tools; that rule is not repeated in the record because the listed Intro to Wheel term runs longer. Refund, waitlist and drop-in rules are on the class policies page and are summarized only briefly. Kids summer camps are for ages 6 and up. Operation Mud (clay workshops for veterans) and the Travel Program are not described here because no schedule is given.

records.name: Cobbs Creek Ambassadors
records.summary: Volunteers who clean up and care for Cobbs Creek Park. They run registered cleanups by zone, hand out plants, and host a yearly summer festival at Whitby Park.
records.what_you_do: Register for a cleanup through the group's Register link, then meet your zone's ambassador at the listed spot. Past cleanups have collected from a few bags up to 71 bags of litter.

schedule.text: Each cleanup zone has a monthly cleanup, usually 9 to 11 am on a Saturday or 2 to 4 pm on a Sunday, starting at a set meeting spot. Some zones meet every other month.

locations.label: Cobbs Creek Park (cleanup spots vary by zone)

cost.text: The page does not list a cost for cleanups. The yearly summer festival is described as offering free food and live music, and all are welcome.

first_step.how: Pick your zone on the Schedule and Map page at cobbscreekparkambassadors.org, register for an upcoming cleanup through the Register link, and meet your zone's ambassador at the listed spot. Email CobbsCreekParkAmbassadors@gmail.com with questions.
first_step.basis: The Schedule and Map page says the group loves new volunteers, and it explains how to start: choose a zone, register, and meet the ambassador at the listed spot.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each cleanup runs about two hours, usually 9 to 11 am on a Saturday or 2 to 4 pm on a Sunday, and starts at a meeting spot named by cross streets. Each zone has its own ambassador, and the group welcomes new volunteers. The page does not list costs, what to bring, or what the group supplies.
first_visit_tips: Email the zone's ambassador or the group address before you come, since the page does not say what to bring or wear.
Meeting spots are cross streets, such as Upland Street and Cobbs Creek Parkway for zone 14.
The Schedule and Map page links a SEPTA route for each zone, starting from 40th and Spruce.

records.notes: The Whitby Park summer festival was Saturday, September 12, 2026, 11 am to 3 pm, with a rain date of September 13, so it is past and is not in the schedule text. The registration link was not opened, since it is a shortened link to a form. Some pages on the site link a .com domain; this record uses the .org address from tier 1. Facebook and Instagram are linked from the site but were not read. Zone 14 gives a personal phone number on the schedule page, which was not recorded. The 700 Cobbs Creek Pkwy address is from tier 1 (city data), not from a group page; the group's pages give cross streets for each zone. Tier 1 said past cleanups collected up to 71 bags, which the group's pages did not re-check.

records.name: Collaborative Cataloging Japan
records.summary: A nonprofit that preserves and shares Japanese experimental film and video. It runs an online viewing library, publishes essays and books, holds exhibitions, and hosts artist talks.
records.what_you_do: Watch works in the online viewing library, join the members' viewings and the monthly feature, or attend a public screening or talk when one is scheduled. The site does not mention classes, workshops or volunteer jobs.

schedule.text: Members get a new monthly feature on the online viewing platform, and each members' viewing usually runs about a month. Public screenings and artist talks are scheduled as events, some in person in Philadelphia.

cost.text: Membership is $5 a month and includes the monthly feature and members' viewings, with discounts on special programs. The page does not name the currency. Individual event prices are not listed.

first_step.how: Browse the online viewing library and the blog, then join with the Become a Member link to get the monthly feature and members' viewings. Public in-person screenings are listed on the Events page, so check there for a date to attend.
first_step.basis: Anyone can see the membership sign up link, and public screenings are listed on the Events page. The page does not say whether non-members can watch the library.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most of the group's work happens online. Members watch a monthly feature and members' viewings on the group's online viewing platform, and each viewing usually runs about a month. Public events include in-person screenings in Philadelphia and artist talks, with dates and years on the Events page. The page does not say how long talks last or whether they are free.
first_visit_tips: Check the Events page for in-person screenings in Philadelphia before you plan a visit, since dates change.
Send questions to the director using the contact page.

records.notes: The contact page shows placeholder text for the street address and phone number, so those were ignored. The office address 5927 Pulaski Ave comes from tax data in the batch and is not confirmed on the group's site; it is labeled simply as Office, and should be checked before publishing. The director's email is readable on the contact page and is recorded. Events page lists public in-person screenings in Philadelphia in late September 2026 and members' viewings from 2024 to 2026. Venue partners named there (Lightbox Film Center, Asian Arts Initiative) were not fetched and have no links on the pages read, so they are not in leads_only. Japanese and English pages exist for About and Programs, which is why both languages are listed.
